what: Merge pass steps 2 and 3: the consistency check of the 27 units, with four finders (registry and notes, links, conventions, repeated facts) and a skeptic for each
ran: The registry and links finders ran on 29 October 2026; the conventions and facts finders and the four skeptics on 10 November 2026. The findings refer to the units as of commit 6c817f1.

finding.path: games-r3.md > Damage and armour maps > 'Tempest Rising armour' bullet (line 89); unit armour/class, armour/notes, uncertain armour/class
finding.summary: The Tempest Rising armour note says the infobox label alone decides the class. That overrides the soldier rule, which wins over every step. The Line Officer's game data gives him tougher infantry armour than the Field Scout, so he should be light, not unarmoured.
finding.evidence: Line Officer wiki infobox (wikitext via API; the page is verified at 1.4.0): armortype Infantry, with a quarter resisted against Rifle, Explosive, Fire and Sniper damage. Its changelog says the Sniper resistance was added in patch 1.2.0+46089. The Field Scout's infobox resists no Rifle damage and lists only the Rocket and Cannon resistances. The Dynasty Guard's matches the Field Scout's. The 2.0.0 patch page changes only his range. The soldier rule in vocabularies.md (armour-class tie-breaks) wins over every step: a soldier whose game data gives a tougher infantry armour type or attribute than the basic rifle infantry is light. The Generals note sets a gunfire test for this same rule, but the TR note instead says the label is enough. The unit's armour.notes says 'Step 1 decided ... the registry reads the class from that label'. j06 hesitations[17] and unclear_rules[2] report following the note against the rule. Other batch soldiers checked: the Drone Operator (infobox resists no Rifle damage) and the Enlightened (same) stay unarmoured.
finding.fix: games-r3.md line 89. Old: 'Units also have six armour percentages, but the label is enough for the class.' New: 'Units also have six armour percentages. For vehicles and aircraft the label is enough for the class. For the soldier rule, a soldier of the Infantry type has tougher armour than the Field Scout, and so is light, when its percentages let less Rifle or Sniper damage through than his (he resists neither). One that resists only Rocket and Cannon damage, as he does, stays unarmoured, and side-wide doctrines such as Body Armor stay out.' Recode tempest-rising.dynasty.line-officer: armour.class unarmoured -> light. Rewrite armour.notes to say the soldier rule decided: step 1 gave unarmoured, but he resists a quarter of Rifle and Sniper damage where the Field Scout resists none. Rewrite uncertain armour/class to name the note. No other batch unit changes.

verdict.reason: Confirmed. The Line Officer's infobox gives him Rifle, Explosive, Fire and Sniper resistances where the Field Scout has none. The vocabularies.md soldier rule wins over every step and makes such a soldier light. games-r3.md line 89 lets the label alone decide, and the coder followed the note against the rule. Of the batch units, only the Line Officer changes.
verdict.evidence: Cached wikitext, at scratch folder facts/pages/tr__Line_Officer and others. Line Officer: armortype Infantry; resists rifle 25, rocket 75, explosive 25, cannon 75, fire 25, sniper 25; the changelog says patch 1.2.0 added the sniper 25. Field Scout, Dynasty Guard (fetched to verify-registry/pages/tr__Dynasty_Guard.wikitext), Drone Operator and Enlightened resist only rocket 75 and cannon 75. Patches 2.0.0 and 2.0.2 change only his range. The unit is coded armour.class unarmoured, its notes credit step 1 and the note, and its uncertain entry flags the soldier rule. j06 hesitations[17] and unclear_rules[2] confirm. Survey of 28 more TR infantry pages: Grenadier and Ignitor (rifle 25), Commando and Sniper (sniper 25 only) would also be lifted by the proposed test. None of them is in the batch.
verdict.better_fix: Keep the recode and the gist of the note fix, and tighten the test. Under 'Rifle or Sniper', the GDF Sniper, which resists only Sniper damage, becomes light. The Ascended and the Cultivator are mixed cases: they let less Rifle damage through (50) but more Rocket and Cannon damage (50 against the scout's 75). Have the note say how those mixed cases go: 'tougher' means no resistance below the Field Scout's and at least one above it. Say 'the label is enough' for vehicles, aircraft and the Heavy infantry type, since the armour_map already sends Heavy infantry to light.

finding.path: games-r3.md > Research notes > Generals > 'The 1.04 files' bullet, second sentence (line 372); units armament[].traits, armament[].delivery, related uncertain entries
finding.summary: The Generals note says any term only the 1.04 files would set is not set, with friendly-fire as its example. That contradicts the field rules. A damage radius or a travel speed in any page an uncertain entry names counts for splash and for projectile delivery, and a database page may carry a code. Coders followed the note, so four units lack terms the rules give them.
finding.evidence: fields.md sources[]: 'the sources' are the cited pages plus every page an uncertain entry names and says what it shows, and an uncited database page may carry a code. The splash rule in vocabularies.md: a radius figure in the sources counts. The delivery rule in fields.md: a travel speed in the sources makes a shot projectile. 1.04 Weapon.ini, fetched from TheSuperHackers repository at 6c7f40d: TechnicalRPGWeapon has PrimaryDamageRadius 5 and RadiusDamageAffects includes ALLIES. TechnicalCannonWeapon has radius 25 and ALLIES. SentryDroneGun has WeaponSpeed 600 and no projectile object. AuroraBombWeapon has radius 20 and ALLIES (NOT_SIMILAR). OverlordTankGun has radius 5/10 and ALLIES. Each unit's uncertain entries name Weapon.ini: Technical armament/0/damage and armament/2/summary, Sentry Drone armament/0/delivery, Aurora armament/0/range and armament/0/traits, Overlord roles/secondary. The coders say they followed the note against the rules: j02 hesitations[6] and unclear_rules[6], j04 hesitations[5] and [17], and the Aurora's uncertain armament/0/traits. Current codes: Technical armament[2].traits is [], armament[1].traits is [splash]; Sentry Drone armament[0].delivery is hitscan; Aurora armament[0].traits is [splash]; Overlord armament[0].traits is [splash]. The note's other examples agree with the rules: the magazine rule rejects a clip size alone, and mount is a proposal field.
finding.fix: games-r3.md line 372. Old: 'Any other term only they would set (friendly-fire from a blast that hurts allies, magazine from a clip size, auto-target from an add-on's own AI) is not set; mention the fact in notes.' New: 'A term whose own rule a figure or flag in these files meets is set from them as from any other page an uncertain entry names: splash from a PrimaryDamageRadius above zero, projectile delivery from a WeaponSpeed the file does not mark as effectively instant, and friendly-fire where a weapon with a damage radius lists ALLIES in RadiusDamageAffects. Any other term only they would set (magazine from a clip size alone, which its rule does not accept, or auto-target from an add-on's own AI) is not set; mention the fact in notes.' Recodes: generals.gla.technical armament[2].traits [] -> [splash, friendly-fire] and armament[1].traits [splash] -> [splash, friendly-fire]; drop the uncertain armament/2/summary clause about the radius not being coded. generals.usa.sentry-drone armament[0].delivery hitscan -> projectile, and rewrite uncertain armament/0/delivery. generals.usa.aurora-bomber armament[0].traits [splash] -> [splash, friendly-fire], and rewrite uncertain armament/0/traits. generals.china.overlord armament[0].traits [splash] -> [splash, friendly-fire] (its source set names Weapon.ini). Rerun the validator for any new atypical lines.

verdict.reason: Confirmed. The fields.md sources[] rule counts every page an uncertain entry names, and the splash and delivery rules accept a radius or a travel speed from those sources. Line 372 bans every term that only the 1.04 files would set. All four units name Weapon.ini in their uncertain entries, the values in the file are as the finding states, and the coders say they followed the note against the rules.
verdict.evidence: Weapon.ini fetched from TheSuperHackers at 6c7f40d (scratch verify-registry/pages/gen/Weapon.ini), plus EA's Weapon.cpp. TechnicalRPGWeapon: radius 5, MinimumAttackRange 5, ALLIES. TechnicalCannonWeapon: radius 25, ALLIES. SentryDroneGun: WeaponSpeed 600, ProjectileObject NONE, radius 0. AuroraBombWeapon: radius 20, ALLIES with NOT_SIMILAR. OverlordTankGun: radius 5/10, ALLIES, ClipSize 2. Weapon.cpp gives a weapon with no projectile and a finite speed delayed damage (distance over speed). Its default RadiusDamageAffects (line 295) includes ALLIES. Current codes are as the finding states. Coder reports: j02 hesitations[6] and unclear_rules[6], j04 hesitations[5] and [17]. The other batch Generals weapons (Jarmen Kell's rifle, the Red Guard's rifle, the Overlord's gattling) have radius 0 and instant speed, so they do not change.
verdict.better_fix: Same recodes. Three wording changes. (a) ALLIES is the engine default, so say 'where a weapon with a damage radius lists ALLIES in RadiusDamageAffects, or has no such line'. (b) Don't claim the magazine rule 'does not accept' a clip size. The magazine rule does accept a clip count in some cases, so keep the old neutral example ('magazine from a clip size'). (c) Decide on the Technical rocket's MinimumAttackRange 5, which the coder listed as an alternative: either set the min-range term from the same files under the same principle, or say why not.

finding.path: games-r3.md > Game-wide mechanics > Tempest Rising > 'Servitor spawns and Arcing' bullet (line 291); Thunderhead abilities/2/kind, Vimana abilities/5/kind
